name: scenario-blender-blockout
description: "Use when a text brief or a reference image must become a Blender blockout whose playblast guides a render-to-real video pass (a video model that takes a reference clip, such as Seedance, or the Render Video lane of the Scenario Blender Plugin): graybox or previs built for a video model, color-coded proxies at metric scale from rough to detailed, density levels from a simple shot to an expert scene with crowds, traffic and many cuts, character stand-ins chosen per video model (colored capsules, capsules with signature features, rigged gray mannequins), a camera locked to the timeline, rail or tracking camera rigs, lens per shot, framing and occlusion checks, a playblast, a hand-off sheet for the video prompt. Also when a render-to-real pass renders the proxies as boxes, reads one figure as two people, gives runners a stiff, lockstep or sliding gait, swaps a car's front and rear, drifts at the end, or the guide camera pops on a cut."
license: MIT
---

# Blender blockout for a render-to-real video pass

The blockout is the guide clip: the video model copies the camera path, framing, lens feel, easing,
cut points, shot lengths, the position and scale of every mass, figure facing and every trajectory,
and it invents the rest from text and images (materials, light, weather, what each proxy really is,
faces, wardrobe, extras, sound). So the blockout has full authority over motion and layout and none
over look. Ambiguity ruins the pass; crudeness does not: a bent lamppost comes back as a snake,
loose limb blocks as extra people, an unmarked car driving backward. Fix identity in geometry first,
in prompt text second, and judge the result on a synced side-by-side of playblast and video, never
in the viewport alone. If a sibling skill named here is missing from your available skills, load it
with `skill_get` (Scenario MCP) or ask the user to install it
(https://github.com/scenario-labs/skills#install); unattended, proceed from tool schemas and flag
the gap.

**REQUIRED BACKGROUND:** scenario-blender-expert (execution channel, review loop, 5.2 API changes).
Video generation: `scenario-blender` (the plugin's quote, generate and place flow), the `scenario`
skill (connection, uploads, jobs) and `scenario-seedance` (reference-video fields).

Toolkit: [`scripts/bx_blockout.py`](scripts/bx_blockout.py):
`import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "<this skill>/scripts"); [sys.modules.pop(m, None) for m in ("bx_blockout", "bx_kits")]; import bx_blockout as B`,
where `<this skill>` is the installed folder's absolute path. The pop drops a copy an earlier run
left in Blender's one Python. Builders are get-or-create by name, so a call can run again, and they
refuse a name the user's own work already holds (names are global to the file). An empty audit
result is a pass. The module docstring shows the call order.
[`scripts/bx_kits.py`](scripts/bx_kits.py) (`import bx_kits as K`, same rules) adds buildings,
stalls, trees, lamps, rocks and vehicles at three fidelity tiers, figures in four cast styles,
crowds, traffic, color schemes and `K.audit_budget`. Four worked scenes, simple to expert, with
render-pass results: [examples](references/examples.md) ([harness](scripts/examples/ex_common.py),
[1](scripts/examples/ex1_watchmaker.py), [2](scripts/examples/ex2_saltflat.py),
[3](scripts/examples/ex3_bridge.py), [4](scripts/examples/ex4_sky_islands.py)).

**Which skill.** This one: guides for a video model. Story previs and animatics judged by a director
and an editor: scenario-blender-previs-storyboard; an approved animatic that must guide a video
model is rebuilt here.

## 1. Restate the brief as a build plan

Before any call, write down:

- **Elements and their primitive**: "bus = long box with a marked front", "figures = colored
  capsules". Never model past what the brief names.
- **Dimensions** in meters for everything; when the brief is silent, take them from
  [the contract tables](references/contract.md) and say so.
- **Format**: integer fps, aspect, seconds. The range is 1 to fps x seconds (8 s at 24 fps: 1..192).
- **Shots**: count, move, lens, framing invariants ("hero always in frame, full figure"), cut style;
  beats pinned to seconds, converted to frames now.
- **Levels**: density (simple, medium, advanced, expert: footprint, elements, heroes, extras,
  shots), fidelity (rough, shaped, detailed) and color scheme, read off the brief and set apart:
  [levels](references/levels.md). Where the brief is silent (naming only heroes and shots is
  silent): advanced, shaped, category colors, and say so; drop to simple or medium only for one
  actor in one place. Expert means many elements, movers and cuts, never finer blocks.
- **Video model**, now: cast style and prompt grammar depend on it (`list_models` on the plugin
  lane, `recommend` on the hosted route).
- **Cast style** per character ([cast](references/cast.md)): a stand-in with limbs hands the model a
  gait to copy; one without limbs lets it invent body and motion. Default heroes to colored
  capsules, featured (two or three signature features: goggles, a hood, a held lantern) when
  characters must stay apart or carry the story's object; a rigged gray mannequin only when the
  blockout must own limb motion. Tell the user the style chosen, its cost in control, and that the
  others can be A/B tested on a short window.
- **Identity colors**: a hero takes the brief's color ("yellow raincoat": yellow) as the nearest
  `B.PALETTE` color, else the next free one: red, blue, green, yellow, purple, cyan. Two heroes in
  one color, or black, white, gray, brown: [contract](references/contract.md).
- **Deliberate gaps** the video model fills, and **acceptance tests** the brief states: they become
  mandatory audits.

Decide what the brief leaves open and record the decision; do not stop to ask. Spending is the
exception: the user approves every Scenario price (section 6). With a reference image: list its
masses, block them at plausible scale, match camera height and lens, `render_still` from the camera,
compare, adjust until the composition matches, and only then animate.

## 2. Output contract

Four deliverables: the scene, a locked camera timeline, the playblast, the hand-off sheet.

- **Scene hygiene.** Role prefixes (`ENV_`, `FIG_`, `PRP_`, `CAM_`, `CRV_`, `RIG_`, `NULL_target_`,
  full table in the contract), one root collection with role sub-collections. Park the default Cube,
  Light and Camera with `B.park`, never delete. If the file holds other work, build in a new scene
  (`B.make_scene`) and touch nothing existing; every object must trace to one of your stages.
- **Scale.** Meters, Z up, ground at z = 0, figure roots at the feet. The model keeps every mass
  where it is at its size, mistakes included. Nothing familiar for scale: add a `REF_` figure.
- **Color separates masses and names identities.** One saturated color per hero (`B.PALETTE`), the
  set in one `K.scheme` (category hues by default, identity grays, or material colors), extras in
  mid grays, one light, a dark world. `B.paint` and the kits set object color and materials; a kit
  carries several colors, so Solid view needs color type Material (`B.solid_view()`'s default and
  the playblast's). An all-gray playblast has lost identity. Recolor a kit through its arguments:
  its materials are shared per color. Grid or checker texture only where the camera travels and
  depth must read, declared "replace, never inherit" in the sheet.
- **Timeline.** `B.lock_format` before any geometry: integer fps, frames 1 to fps x seconds,
  1920x1080 (2520x1080 for 21:9) at 100 %. One camera per shot, bound to a `CUT_` marker on its
  first frame (`B.bind_cuts`), hard cuts, zero transition frames.
- **Camera rigs.** Rail: `B.rail_camera` (curve, dolly on Follow Path, aim with Track To, camera).
  Handheld tracking, straight push-in and multi-shot masters: recipes in the contract. Reframe by
  moving the aim target, never by rotating the camera.
- **Lens.** One lens per shot from shot size (`B.lens_for_coverage`; 28 mm orbits, 42 to 45 mm
  over-the-shoulder, 24 to 30 mm interiors, 85 mm macro), `clip_start` 0.05. A cut changes lens only
  by changing camera: never key a lens step on a cut frame. A lens may ease inside a shot (a
  deliberate zoom), never jump.
- **Easing.** Bezier keys with auto-clamped handles (`B.smooth_keys`); speed is key spacing on the
  rail (`B.key_rail`), a pause is two near-equal values. LINEAR only for per-frame baked travel
  (vehicles, wheels). Keys run past every cut so nothing stops on the boundary.
- **Handheld** is NOISE F-curve modifiers, never keyed jitter. Measure the result with
  `B.audit_handheld` against the budget in the contract; `animation_data_clear()` removes the
  modifiers, so re-add them after rekeying.

## 3. Channel: the plugin or headless

The live channel is the plugin's local Scenario MCP server, `scenario-blender` (the guide at
[blender.scenario.com](https://blender.scenario.com/) calls the plugin Scenario for Blender). Tool
table, call limits and recovery after a timeout: [plugin](references/plugin.md). The two that bite
first: `execute_python` stays off until the user enables **Allow connected agents to run Python** (a
`PermissionError` means ask), and a call stops after 120 s, so send one stage piece per call and run
`B.stage_backup(label)` after each stage.

**The plugin's own tools** ([plugin](references/plugin.md)): its paid **Blockout** suits a generic
Stage 2 set, with no figures, cameras or identity colors; **`camera_path`** keys one shot around a
static center, never tracking or multi-shot (`B.rail_camera`); **Render Video** is the video pass.

**Headless**, with no plugin: run each stage through scenario-blender-expert's headless helper. Load
the preceding `.blend`, check it with `B.guard`, extend it, then save a new `B.stage_backup(label)`
for the next stage. The [examples harness](scripts/examples/ex_common.py) is only for one-shot
builds from factory startup: `start()` deletes all objects, including prior stages. Never reuse it
to resume a backup. The 120 s limit is plugin-only.

## 4. Build order

A reset is recovered from the last backup ([contract](references/contract.md)). Every call or stage
script starts with `B.guard(expected_file=..., scene=...)`: queued calls land in whatever file is
open.

0. **Probe**, read-only: `scene_summary`, `datablocks_summary` (headless: `bpy.data`). Other work
   present: new scene.
1. **Format and scaffolding**: `B.make_scene`, `B.lock_format`, `B.collection` tree, `B.park`, dark
   world.
2. **Set**: kits at the chosen fidelity (`K.building`, `K.stall`, `K.tree`) or thick boxes (`B.box`)
   at true scale, repeats as linked duplicates (`K.instance`). Or the plugin Blockout for a generic
   set.
3. **Figures**: `K.figure(..., style=, features=)` per hero in the chosen cast style, root at the
   feet, facing along travel ([cast](references/cast.md)). Travel with `K.walk_path` from a table of
   (frame, position), stride 0.42 x height for a walk, about 0.7 for a run; gestures with `K.pose`;
   extras with `K.crowd(style=...)`.
4. **Props and vehicles**: literal primitives at true position. Mark a vehicle's front in geometry
   (light blocks and grille in front, dark red behind); wheels at z = radius (kit wheels: body
   mesh). Spinning wheels, cyclists ([contract](references/contract.md)): `K.drive` a `"bicycle"`
   `K.vehicle`, `K.pedal` its rider, never `K.walk_path`. No loose blocks near a figure.
5. **Light**: one area light; named key, fill, rim only when the brief designs light.
6. **Cameras**: rigs and lenses per shot, `B.bind_cuts`.
7. **Motion polish**: `B.key_rail` and `B.smooth_keys`, keys past cuts, handheld, vehicle travel as
   one monotone curve keyed per frame.
8. **Audit** (section 5) until clean. When set dressing hides the hero, move the blockers and keep
   the camera plan.
9. **Finalize**: frame 1, shot 1's camera, `B.audit_frames`, `B.state_audit`, final backup, then
   playblast and hand-off sheet.

## 5. Audits: numbers judge, then look

| Check                                | Helper                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame math and resolution            | `B.audit_frames(seconds, fps)`                                                |
| Markers bound, switches, lens, jumps | `B.audit_cuts()` (`same_lens_across_cuts=True` when the brief wants one lens) |
| Subjects in frame per shot           | `B.audit_framing({"CAM_s1": ["FIG_red"]}, whole=True)` for full figures       |
| Head never hidden                    | `B.audit_occlusion("FIG_red")`                                                |
| Too close, outside the legal volume  | `B.audit_distance(subject, volume=...)` (full-figure shots only)              |
| Interpenetration                     | `B.audit_intersections(names)`                                                |
| Feet and wheels on the ground        | `B.audit_ground(names)`                                                       |
| Handheld amplitude                   | `B.audit_handheld("CAM_s1")`                                                  |
| Census before hand-off               | `B.state_audit()`                                                             |

Audit each shot's own subject (the wheel for a macro, the hand for an insert). Then look:
`set_frame` and `render_still` at the first, middle and last frame of every shot, and check what
numbers miss: a vehicle's front, connected figures, rigid props without organic curves, nothing
stray at frame edges, an ending as locked as the opening. Thresholds and readings:
[audits](references/audits.md). An audit samples every `step` frames; on a long shot raise `step` to
stay under the call limit.

## 6. Playblast, hand-off sheet, video pass

**Playblast.** Headless, on the latest `B.stage_backup` copy, with scenario-blender-expert's
`bx_review.playblast(out_path, res_pct=100)`: an H.264 MP4 of the scene camera over the frame range
in Workbench, cuts following the bound markers. Use the session's binary (`bpy.app.binary_path`): an
older `blender` on PATH refuses the file. With no shell, the same call through `execute_python`
blocks Blender while it renders: keep it to short clips, and after a timeout look for the file
before running it again. Add camera stills at each shot's start, middle and end.

**Hand-off sheet**, built from the scene ([template](references/handoff.md)):

- color legend tied to reference images and garments;
- `K.cast()` rows, the cut list from `B.cut_list()` with exact times;
- which entities are blocked and which exist only in words;
- every artifact with its timecode, each motion state in words ("creeps", "stands still");
- tie-break clauses ("if text and video disagree about motion, the video wins").

**Video pass**, always through Scenario, after the user approves the exact price. Unattended, stop
at the quote (`estimate_cost` or `dry_run`), report it, and skip local uploads that need the user's
file choice:

- **Plugin, Render Video lane**: `B.solid_view()` so the capture shows identity colors,
  `force_solid` false (it turns everything one gray), a timeline length the model accepts, then
  `list_models`, `model_schema`, `render_form` (`configure` with `parameters`
  `{"duration": <clip seconds>}`, `prepare`, `inspect`), `estimate_cost`, `generate`, `wait_for_job`
  and the result application, steps in [handoff](references/handoff.md) Route 1. The capture is a
  silent 1280x720 clip.
- **Hosted Scenario MCP**, for the full-resolution playblast: upload the playblast as the `scenario`
  skill shows, discover a model that takes a reference video, `model_schema_get`, `model_run` with
  `dry_run` first, `jobs_wait`, `asset_download`.

Write the prompt motion-first: the clip is rehearsal footage, the cast is described by role and
motion, never by the proxies' shapes, and style comes from a four-panel style board rather than one
restyled frame. A capsule cast adds a stand-in clause (the capsules only mark position, height, pace
and heading) and a gait clause ([cast](references/cast.md)). On the plugin lane the plugin states
the clip's and images' roles itself, so `look` holds only cast and style. Grammar, clauses and
tested limits: [handoff](references/handoff.md).

## Worked example

Brief: "10 s, 24 fps: a red runner sprints between crate rows toward camera in a warehouse; a blue
guard steps out at second 6; handheld 35 mm backing away."

1. `scene_summary` `{"fields": ["type"], "limit": 100}`: the file holds other work, so build beside
   it.
2. `execute_python`: `B.make_scene("BLK_warehouse")`; next call `B.guard(scene="BLK_warehouse")`,
   `B.lock_format(24, 10)` (1..240), collections, backup.
3. Floor 34 x 20 m, 7 m walls, two rows of 1.2 m crates with `B.box`; backup.
4. `K.figure("red", 1.8, (0, 15, 0), style="featured", features=("hood",))`, then `K.walk_path` to
   (0, 1) by frame 200 with a sprint's stride (1.3 m); the blue guard, a capsule, steps into the
   aisle over frames 144 to 156; backup.
5. `B.rail_camera("s1", [(0, 3, 1.5), (0, -1, 1.5), (0, -4, 1.5)], follow="FIG_red", target_offset=(0, 0, 1.2), lens=35)`,
   `B.key_rail("RIG_dolly_s1", [(1, 0), (260, 1)])`, `B.bind_cuts([(1, "CAM_s1")])`, handheld noise
   within budget.
6. `B.audit_frames(10, 24)`, `B.audit_cuts()`,
   `B.audit_framing({"CAM_s1": ["FIG_red", "FIG_blue"]}, whole=True)`,
   `B.audit_occlusion("FIG_red")`, `B.audit_handheld("CAM_s1")`; move crates until clean.
7. `set_frame` 1, 120, 240 with `render_still` each, and look. Backup, headless playblast,
   `B.cut_list()` into the sheet.

## Common mistakes and downstream misreads

- **Identity not in geometry**: a floating head or slab arms; loose blocks near a figure read as
  extra people; a car with no marked front driven in reverse; an occupant behind an opaque cabin
  vanishes (give the cabin alpha).
- **Camera grammar**: a key on the cut frame freezes motion there; an overhead orbit read as a cut;
  seats mirrored on a reverse camera; invented reverse shots in dialogue; drift in the last seconds.
- **Ambiguous motion**: slow proxy motion reads as either rolling or still; the sheet decides.
- **Copied limbs**: on a reference-video model, stepped or looped legs come back stiff, in lockstep
  or sliding; switch that character to a capsule ([cast](references/cast.md)).
- **Fragile detail**: sub-pixel parts change identity between restyles; a style that implies text
  invents gibberish lettering.
- **Opening-frame fiction**: "starts at the door" needs a doorway behind frame 1; high shots over
  flat ground read flat.
- **State drift**: render probes that leave resolution or file path changed; pre-existing objects
  adopted as your own; Blender 5 slotted actions hiding F-curves (use `B.fcurves`).

# Blender expert (router and agent protocol)

Expert-level Blender work is a loop, not a script: build big to small, and at every stage turn the
model, measure it and fix it before adding detail. This skill is the protocol every Blender task
follows and the map to the domain skills distilled from Blender Studio artists, Blender Conference
talks and top instructors (sources in each skill). If a sibling skill named here is missing from
your available skills, load it with `skill_get` (Scenario MCP) or ask the user to install it
(https://github.com/scenario-labs/skills#install); unattended, proceed from tool schemas and flag
the gap.

## 1. Execution channel

- **Live GUI Blender** (user's session over the MCP bridge), for anything interactive: real
  sculpt/paint brushes, weight painting, viewport screenshots. One short, idempotent script per call
  returning a compact result dict. Get-or-create by name. Never touch objects you did not create.
  Save a stage backup `bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=..., copy=True)` after each stage.
- **Headless helper** `blender -b [file] --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 -P x.py -- args`,
  for renders, audits, batch ops, anything when no bridge is up. Use `--factory-startup` so the
  user's add-ons and preferences stay out of the run (an add-on can call the network or change
  defaults); the Scenario Blender Plugin's headless server,
  `blender --background scene.blend --command scenario_blender`, is the exception because it needs
  the extension loaded. Without `--python-exit-code` a failing script still exits 0. Print a final
  machine-readable result line.

Never open your own GUI Blender window to test things on the user's machine: windows steal focus and
pile up. Live work goes through the user's already-running Blender; everything else runs headless,
one Blender process at a time per agent (other sessions may be rendering on the same machine).

**Live channel: the Scenario Blender Plugin.** When the user's Blender runs the Scenario Blender
Plugin, its local MCP server `scenario-blender` is the bridge. Setup, quotes, generation and placing
results are the `scenario-blender` skill's work; this section covers the bpy side (guide at
[blender.scenario.com](https://blender.scenario.com/)). Its tool names differ from other Blender MCP
servers: there is no `execute_blender_code`, `get_scene_info`, `get_viewport_screenshot` or
`import_asset`.

| Step                          | Plugin tool and main arguments                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Read the scene before acting  | `scene_summary`, then `object_detail` with `name` for one object and `datablocks_summary` for counts                                           |
| Check an API before scripting | `blender_api_help` with `path`, such as `bpy.types.BevelModifier`                                                                              |
| Run bpy                       | `execute_python` with `code`; `bpy` and `result = {}` are preloaded, so fill `result`                                                          |
| Look                          | `screenshot_viewport` (viewport with overlays), `render_still` with `source` (`CAMERA` or `VIEWPORT`), `width` and `height`; both need the GUI |
| Select, move the timeline     | `select_objects` with `names` (a list), `set_frame` with `frame`                                                                               |

Read each tool's input schema from the server before its first call: it is the reference for
optional arguments.

- `execute_python` stays off until the user enables **Allow connected agents to run Python** in the
  plugin preferences. A `PermissionError` means ask for it or stay on the specific tools. A refused
  spelling (quit, factory reset, file deletion) changed nothing: rewrite the call.
- Budget every call: the plugin stops a call after 120 s and some agent clients stop waiting after
  60 s. Make one logical change per call, so one Undo reverts it, and send bakes, QuadriFlow on
  dense meshes, turntables, playblasts and final renders to a headless Blender working on a saved
  copy.
- A timed-out call has an unknown outcome: read the scene again before retrying, never resend it
  blindly.
- The plugin's tools never save the user's own file. The live channel's stage backup
  (`save_as_mainfile(..., copy=True)` through `execute_python`) writes a separate file and leaves
  the open file and its unsaved state alone: it is also the saved copy that headless work starts
  from. Ask the user to save their own file at milestones; with no one to ask, keep working from the
  copies and say in the report that the open file is still unsaved.

Check `bpy.app.version` first; this skill set targets 5.2 LTS, while the Scenario Blender Plugin
also runs on 5.0 and 5.1 (`scene_summary` reports the version), so check the version timeline in the
deltas before using a recent API. Many tutorials the experts recorded use 2.8x to 4.2 UI: read
[`references/blender-5.2-deltas.md`](references/blender-5.2-deltas.md) before trusting any
remembered operator, brush name or API.

**Verified capability matrix (Blender 5.2.1):**

| Action                                                                                                                                | Headless                                               | GUI session                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Voxel remesh, QuadriFlow, multires subdivide, modifiers, bmesh, UV ops with edit-mode context, Cycles/EEVEE/Workbench renders, baking | yes                                                    | yes                                               |
| `bpy.ops.brush.asset_activate`, dyntopo toggle                                                                                        | yes                                                    | yes                                               |
| Brush strokes (`sculpt.brush_stroke`, `paint.image_paint`, `paint.weight_paint`)                                                      | no (poll fails)                                        | yes, via [`scripts/bx_gui.py`](scripts/bx_gui.py) |
| `paint.mask_flood_fill`, `sculpt.mesh_filter`                                                                                         | CRASHES Blender                                        | yes, via `bx_gui.run()`                           |
| Programmatic sculpting on mesh data                                                                                                   | yes, `scenario-blender-sculpting/scripts/bx_sculpt.py` | yes                                               |

## 2. The expert loop (every domain)

1. **Establish the brief** in numbers: purpose (film, game engine, still, animation), budgets (tris,
   texture size, frame range), style (stylized or realistic), references. When the brief is silent,
   choose a documented default from the domain skill and write it down.
2. **Plan the stages** the domain skill defines. Never start with detail.
3. **Build one stage** with the smallest scripts that do it.
4. **Gate the stage:** run the measurable checks ([`scripts/bx_audit.py`](scripts/bx_audit.py) for
   meshes, the domain's own checks) AND render a review sheet
   ([`scripts/bx_review.py`](scripts/bx_review.py): silhouette, matcap, wire from
   front/side/three-quarter/low) and open it with the image reader. Experts orbit constantly; the
   review sheet is the agent's orbit. Every image read stays in the agent's context: for quick looks
   use `render_still` at about 768 px wide or `screenshot_viewport`, and keep review sheets near
   1600 px (`res=400` for four views and three modes). Judge with the domain's
   `references/critique.md`.
5. **Fix before advancing.** A problem found at blockout costs one script; found after texturing it
   costs the stage.
6. **Deliver with evidence:** run the delivery gate (`bx_audit.deliverable`, below) on the parts of
   the asset before any export or handoff and fix every error. Then report final renders, gate and
   audit numbers, and what was not verified.

Never report a model, rig, animation or render as done without having looked at a render of it.

## 3. Persona pipelines

| Persona / brief                                     | Skill chain                                                                                                                                                                                                | Deliverable                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Character artist, stylized or realistic             | scenario-blender-sculpting, scenario-blender-retopology, scenario-blender-uv-baking, scenario-blender-texturing-shading, scenario-blender-hair                                                             | sculpt, animation-ready low poly, UVs, baked maps, materials |
| AI-mesh finisher (Scenario 3D output to production) | gate the generated asset, scenario-blender-retopology (or cleanup + remesh), scenario-blender-uv-baking (bake FROM the generated high), scenario-blender-texturing-shading; generation itself: scenario-3d | clean, UV'd, baked asset at a stated budget                  |
| Game asset artist                                   | scenario-blender-hard-surface or scenario-blender-sculpting, scenario-blender-retopology (game budget), scenario-blender-uv-baking, scenario-blender-texturing-shading, scenario-blender-export            | low poly + PBR set, exported glTF/FBX                        |
| Rigger / character TD                               | scenario-blender-rigging                                                                                                                                                                                   | rig with controls, weights, deformation tests                |
| Animator                                            | scenario-blender-previs-storyboard (shot planning), scenario-blender-animation                                                                                                                             | blocked, splined, polished shot + playblast                  |
| Story / previs artist                               | scenario-blender-previs-storyboard, scenario-blender-grease-pencil                                                                                                                                         | shots, cameras, animatic                                     |
| Look-dev and lighting artist                        | scenario-blender-texturing-shading, scenario-blender-lighting-rendering                                                                                                                                    | lit, color-managed, composited renders                       |

| 2D / 2.5D animator                                  | scenario-blender-grease-pencil                                                                                                                                                                             | GP animation                                                 |

Related skills outside this set: scenario-3d (generate meshes to finish here), scenario-textures (AI
textures).

## 4. Shared toolkit (`scripts/`, all tested on 5.2.1)

- `bx_audit.py`: `audit(obj, high=None)` returns quads %, n-gons, poles (valence 3 / 5+ / 6+),
  non-manifold, loose, duplicates, flipped faces, self-intersections, boundary loops, symmetry %,
  edge-length CV, and fidelity to a high poly; `verdict(report)` lists problems. CLI:
  `blender -b f.blend --python bx_audit.py -- --object Name [--high Sculpt] [--json out.json]`.
- `bx_audit.deliverable(objs, profile="game")`: the delivery gate. `audit` grades topology; this
  grades what an engine, renderer or slicer receives, across the parts of ONE asset:
  - errors in every profile: a mesh with no faces after modifiers, floating parts and fragments,
    closed parts inside out, negative scale; z-fighting between parts everywhere but `print`;
  - by profile (`game`, `render`, `print`, `roblox`): unapplied scale, faces pointing into a part
    (an error from 0.1% of its surface, a warning below except for `print`), duplicate faces, no UV
    map under an image texture, open borders for `print` and `roblox`, any gap between parts for
    `print`, the Roblox 20,000-triangle mesh limit (checked 2026-10-18).
  - Returns `{pass, errors, warnings, per_object}`. Tolerances scale with the asset's diagonal.
    UV-seam splits from a glTF import are welded for the checks, so seams never read as holes.
  - Gate separate props one by one: every prop but the largest reads as floating.
  - CLI, exit code 2 on failure:
    `blender -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 -P bx_audit.py -- --deliverable [--import model.glb | --objects A B] --profile game [--json out.json]`.
  - Fixes: apply scale (`obj.data.transform(Matrix.Diagonal(obj.scale).to_4x4())`, then
    `obj.scale = (1, 1, 1)`; a scale the message puts on a parent: select the parent and its
    children, `bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)`), `bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals` for
    inside-out parts, `bmesh.ops.reverse_faces` for faces pointing inward
    (`per_object[name]["inward_faces_at"]`), delete or offset the hidden face of a z-fighting pair,
    join or move floating parts, delete fragments.
  - Engines cull back faces: to see what they draw, render
    `bx_review.review(parts, out, culling=True)` (magenta shows through a face pointing inward) and
    compare with a sheet without.
- `bx_review.py`: `review(objs, out_dir, views, modes, culling=False)` takes objects or names and
  writes one contact sheet (rows = modes, cols = views) in a temporary scene, user settings
  untouched; `playblast(out_path, res_pct=50)`; `turntable(obj, out_path, frames=72, res=720)`. Only
  `review` has a command line: call the others from a short wrapper script.
- `bx_gui.py`: real brushes in a live session: `set_view`, `activate_brush(mode, name)`,
  `stroke(mode, world_points, size, strength)`, `run(op, **kw)`, `set_paint_color`, `screenshot`.

Import pattern: `import sys; sys.path.append("<this skill>/scripts"); import bx_audit, bx_review`.
Replace `<this skill>` with the absolute path of the installed skill folder: Blender's Python does
not share the agent's working directory, and over a live bridge the code runs inside the user's
Blender. Check the path in the first call (`result["ok"] = os.path.isdir(path)`) and
`importlib.reload` a module after the skill updates.

## 5. Version traps that break most remembered code

- Brushes are assets (4.3):
  `bpy.ops.brush.asset_activate(asset_library_type='ESSENTIALS', asset_library_identifier="", relative_asset_identifier="brushes/essentials_brushes-mesh_sculpt.blend/Brush/Clay Strips")`;
  brush size is a diameter (5.0); Flatten/Fill/Scrape merged into the Plane type.
- Auto Smooth removed (4.1): `mesh.shade_smooth()` / Smooth by Angle modifier; voxel remesh output
  is flat-shaded until you call `shade_smooth()`.
- Principled BSDF v2 (4.0): address sockets by name; Emission strength defaults to 0.
- `BLENDER_EEVEE` is the EEVEE Next identifier in 5.x (`BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT` fails).
- Compositor is a node group (5.0): `scene.compositing_node_group`, not `scene.node_tree`.
- Video output: set `image_settings.media_type = 'VIDEO'` before `file_format = 'FFMPEG'` (5.0).
- Slotted actions (4.4), `action.fcurves` removed (5.0): use
  `bpy_extras.anim_utils.action_get_channelbag_for_slot(action, slot)`.
- Bone collections replace armature layers (4.0); Grease Pencil v3 is `GREASEPENCIL` with
  `bpy.ops.grease_pencil.*` (4.3).
- Positional context dicts for operators are gone: `with bpy.context.temp_override(...)`.
- `obj.matrix_world` is stale right after setting location/scale until `view_layer.update()`.

## References

- [`references/bpy-reliability.md`](references/bpy-reliability.md): checklist and tested procedures
  for reliable bpy (operators vs data API, stale references, evaluated vs original data, idempotent
  headless jobs, numpy bulk access, node trees, persistence). Load before writing any non-trivial
  script.
- `references/blender-5.2-deltas.md`: full, cited list of what changed from 2.8x to 5.2 per domain
  (load before writing code from memory or following an old tutorial).

# Blender export (engine-ready files)

An export is done when the file has been re-imported and measured, not when the exporter returned
`FINISHED`. Gate the asset first, export with a preset, then round-trip the file. This skill builds
on `scenario-blender-expert` (execution channels, the delivery gate) and imports its scripts, so
install the two side by side. If a sibling skill named here is missing from your available skills,
load it with `skill_get` (Scenario MCP) or ask the user to install it
(https://github.com/scenario-labs/skills#install); unattended, proceed from tool schemas and flag
the gap.

Toolkit: [`scripts/bx_export.py`](scripts/bx_export.py). Per-engine facts with their sources:
[`references/engines.md`](references/engines.md).

## Quick reference

| Target                   | Preset            | File                | Engine side                                |
| ------------------------ | ----------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Unity, static mesh       | `unity`           | FBX                 | import defaults                            |
| Unity, character         | `unity_skeletal`  | FBX                 | leave Bake Axis Conversion off             |
| Unreal Engine            | `unreal`          | FBX                 | Convert Scene Unit (to centimeters)        |
| Unreal Engine, character | `unreal_skeletal` | FBX                 | one root bone                              |
| Godot 4                  | `godot`           | GLB                 | import defaults; Generate LODs in the dock |
| Roblox                   | `roblox`          | FBX                 | 20,000 triangles per mesh                  |
| three.js and the web     | `web`             | GLB, meshopt, WebP  | `MeshoptDecoder`; not for Godot            |
| any glTF reader          | `gltf`            | GLB                 |                                            |
| USD pipelines            | `usd`             | USDC                |                                            |
| Apple AR Quick Look      | `usdz`            | USDZ, 2048 textures |                                            |
| 3D printing              | `print`           | STL in millimeters  | slicer reads millimeters                   |

The Unity and Godot presets were imported into Unity 6000.3 and Godot 4.7.2 and measured; `unreal`,
`unreal_skeletal` and `roblox` follow Epic's and Roblox's documentation and pass the Blender round
trip only. The measurements live in [`references/engines.md`](references/engines.md).

## Procedure

1. **Gate.** Run `bx_audit.deliverable(parts, profile)` from `scenario-blender-expert` and fix every
   error. Scale left on an object travels into the engine as the node's transform.
   - Open borders and edges shared by three or more faces have no automatic fix. On a generated
     chest, hole filling closed 4 of 24 borders and added a back-to-back face.
   - Rebuild the surface with `scenario-blender-retopology`, bake the original's maps onto it, then
     gate again.
   - Without a rebuild, report the file as blocked for that profile (`roblox` requires watertight
     meshes). Never deliver it as ready.
2. **Size and pivot.** A generated mesh arrives at an arbitrary size with its origin at its center,
   so it sinks into the floor. `bxe.ground(parts, width=0.9)` (or `height=`, in meters) bakes the
   transforms, puts the center of the base at the origin and scales to the real size. Ask for the
   size when the brief does not give it; unattended, pick a plausible one and state it as an
   assumption. Static meshes only.
3. **Pick the preset** from the table. Pass every object the file needs: a skinned mesh AND its
   armature, LOD meshes and their group, collision meshes beside their render mesh.
4. **Export:** `bxe.export(path, preset, objects, **overrides)`. Any exporter keyword overrides the
   preset, such as `bake_anim=True` on `roblox` for an animated file. The result records the
   settings used.
   - Before Blender 5.2 the glTF exporter has no meshopt. `web` then writes an uncompressed GLB,
     which loads without `MeshoptDecoder`, and lists the option in `skipped_settings`. Report it to
     the user. Any other setting the exporter lacks raises.
5. **Round-trip:** `bxe.round_trip(path, objects, preset=...)` re-imports the file in a background
   Blender, leaving the open scene alone. It compares size (1 mm), triangles, deforming bones, root
   bones (one expected), armature scale, shape keys, every action stored for the objects, and the
   image maps on each material (base color, metallic, roughness, normal, emission). Then it lists
   every difference. Fix each one, or say why it is expected.
6. **glTF contents:** `bxe.glb_summary(path)` lists `extensions_required`, morph targets, skins,
   clips and image types without Blender. A loader refuses a file that requires an extension it
   lacks.
7. **Engine check:** import into the engine and look. For Godot, the
   [headless check](references/engines.md#headless-check) prints each node's rotation and scale,
   each mesh's size and floor height, and the maps each material received. Full flows:
   `scenario-unity-pipeline-automation`, `scenario-unreal-pipeline-automation`,
   `scenario-godot-pipeline-automation`.

## Scale, axes and units

- Blender works in meters, Z-up, with the asset's front facing -Y. glTF is meters, Y-up
  (`export_yup`). FBX stores its axes as metadata; the presets write -Z forward, Y up.
- Keep `scene.unit_settings.scale_length` at 1.0. Any other value rescales every export.
- Apply object scale before export: `obj.data.transform(Matrix.Diagonal(obj.scale).to_4x4())`, then
  `obj.scale = (1, 1, 1)`, so the engine node imports at scale 1. `bxe.ground()` does it for every
  mesh at once.
- Engines read 1 unit as 1 meter and place an object by its origin. A prop's origin belongs at the
  center of its base, so it stands on the floor where it is placed (step 2).
- FBX scale: `unity` writes `FBX_SCALE_ALL` (Unity reads file scale 1). `unreal` keeps
  `FBX_SCALE_NONE` (Unity reads it as file scale 0.01, a centimeter file). `roblox` uses
  `FBX_SCALE_UNITS`, as Roblox's export requirements ask.
- STL has no unit and slicers read millimeters, so `print` multiplies by 1000.

## Characters

- Export the armature with its meshes. `use_armature_deform_only` leaves control bones out, so keep
  every deforming bone in one hierarchy under one root bone. Unreal's importer reports "Found
  multiple roots. The importer only supports one root per mesh."
- `add_leaf_bones` is off in every preset. Left on, each chain gains an extra end bone that breaks
  retargeting.
- `unity_skeletal` and `unreal_skeletal` bake every action (`bake_anim_use_all_actions`), one clip
  per action. Unity names each clip `Armature|Action` (measured: `Rig|Wave`), so name actions as the
  clips should read. glTF exports each action as an animation under its own name.
- `roblox` exports no animation. For an animated file, pass `bake_anim=True` to `export()` and to
  `round_trip()`, which then compares the actions too.
- Shape keys travel in FBX (blend shapes), glTF (morph targets, names in `extras.targetNames`) and
  USD. Building ARKit or viseme sets is `scenario-blender-rigging`'s work.
- Roblox: at most 4 influences per vertex, bones frozen (scale 1, rotation 0), root at the origin
  with no influences, one animation track per mesh. Check influences with
  `max(len(v.groups) for v in obj.data.vertices)`.

## LODs and collision

- `bxe.lods(obj, ratios=(0.5, 0.25))` renames the mesh `Name_LOD0` and adds decimated `Name_LOD1..n`
  under an empty called `Name`, which takes the mesh's place under its parent. Static meshes only:
  it refuses a skinned mesh. Unity builds the LOD Group from those names. Godot generates LODs at
  import (Generate LODs). Unreal documents "Import LODs", all LODs sharing one pivot. The group
  exports as a plain FBX Null, and Unreal's import of it is unmeasured. It welds the vertices a glTF
  import splits at UV seams before decimating; without the weld, the LODs open into cracks.
- `bxe.collision(obj, engine, shape, max_verts=64)` adds a collision mesh named for the importer:
  - Unreal: `UCX_Name_00` (convex hull) or `UBX_Name_00` (box), exported in the same FBX. Unreal
    skips Auto Generate Collision when the file carries one.
  - Godot: `Name-convcolonly` for `convex` (one hull) and `box` (the bounds, a box collider), or
    `Name-colonly` for `mesh` (the mesh as a trimesh, static bodies only).
  - Unity and Roblox: returns None. Colliders are set in the editor.
  - A convex hull keeps at most `max_verts` vertices, spread over the shape. A generated mesh's full
    hull runs to thousands of faces. 64 is this toolkit's budget, not an engine limit. `None` keeps
    every vertex, and a dense full hull can come out with open edges.
- Decimation can wreck UV seams and silhouettes. Review every LOD with `bx_review` before export.

## Batch conversion

```bash
blender -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 -P bx_export.py -- \
        --batch /abs/in /abs/out --preset godot --profile game
```

For every model in the folder (GLB, glTF, FBX, OBJ, USD, STL, PLY): import into an empty scene, run
the delivery gate, export with the preset, re-import and compare. It writes `/abs/out/report.json`
with each file's gate errors, size, skipped settings and round-trip differences. One failing file
never stops the folder: it gets a `failed` entry. Two inputs sharing a name keep their format in the
output name (`hero_fbx.glb`, `hero_glb.glb`). Open the report before calling the batch done.

## Worked example: a generated GLB to Unity and Godot

```python
import sys
sys.path.append("/abs/skills/scenario-blender-expert/scripts")
sys.path.append("/abs/skills/scenario-blender-export/scripts")
import bpy, bx_audit, bx_export as bxe

bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath="/abs/in/robot.glb")
parts = [o.name for o in bpy.context.scene.objects if o.type == "MESH"]
gate = bx_audit.deliverable(parts, profile="game")
print(gate["errors"])            # fix each one, then gate again until "pass" is True
bxe.ground(parts, height=1.2)    # the robot's real height in meters, base center at the origin

bxe.export("/abs/out/robot.fbx", "unity", parts)
print(bxe.round_trip("/abs/out/robot.fbx", parts, preset="unity")["diffs"])
# ["Robot: material Body lost its Metallic, Roughness maps"]: write them for the engine
print(bxe.extra_maps(parts, "/abs/out", "unity")["written"])
bxe.export("/abs/out/robot.glb", "godot", parts)
print(bxe.glb_summary("/abs/out/robot.glb")["extensions_required"])            # []
```

A generated GLB often holds one object per part, all sharing the asset's pivot. Keep them as
separate objects when the engine should animate or swap parts. Join them (`bpy.ops.object.join` with
the parts selected) for a single static prop, then gate again.

## Common mistakes

- Calling an export done on `FINISHED`. The exporter succeeds on files the engine imports at 100x
  scale or without the skin.
- Exporting a skinned mesh without its armature, or the armature without its mesh.
- Setting Bake Axis Conversion or Apply Transform to remove the armature node's rotation: neither
  removes it, and the first turns the character around.
- The `web` preset for Godot, or any compressed GLB for a loader without its decoder. Check
  `extensions_required` first.
- FBX textures left as external paths: the presets copy and embed them (`path_mode="COPY"`,
  `embed_textures=True`), so the file travels alone. `export()` gives packed images without an
  extension (as a GLB import leaves them) a `.jpg` or `.png` name first. An image never saved (a new
  bake target) or edited since travels as a packed copy of its pixels (`packed_unsaved_images`).
- A textured FBX that shows untextured in Unity: the default import keeps embedded textures inside
  the file. Extract Textures (Materials tab) into the model's folder assigns them.
- Trusting an FBX made from a glTF import for metal and roughness. The glTF importer routes one
  packed image through Separate Color, and the FBX exporter drops both maps: the file re-imports
  with Metallic 0 and Roughness 0.5. Base color, normal and emission travel. `round_trip()` reports
  the loss. `bxe.extra_maps(parts, out_dir, engine)` writes the two maps as files to assign:
  - Unity: `<material>_MetallicSmoothness.png` in the Metallic Map slot (Standard or URP Lit),
    Smoothness Source on Metallic Alpha, sRGB unchecked. Unity's FBX import assigned only the base
    color, even from a file carrying both maps (measured).
  - Roblox and Unreal: `<material>_Metallic.png` and `<material>_Roughness.png`, 8-bit grayscale. On
    Roblox, set them as MetalnessMap and RoughnessMap of a SurfaceAppearance. In Unreal, uncheck
    sRGB on both.
  - Godot: deliver the `godot` GLB, which keeps every map.
- An STL at Blender scale: a 10 cm part prints at 0.1 mm.
- LODs exported without a look: decimation can collapse thin parts.

# Blender Geometry Nodes (procedural systems and simulations)

Expert Geometry Nodes work means thinking in fields evaluated on domains, keeping systems
declarative (data and instructions come in from outside), and shipping tools that artists drive from
modifier inputs without opening the tree. For an agent it also means proving every tree with numbers
read from the evaluated geometry and a render, because the node editor's red links and warnings are
invisible from Python unless you ask for them. If a sibling skill named here is missing from your
available skills, load it with `skill_get` (Scenario MCP) or ask the user to install it
(https://github.com/scenario-labs/skills#install); unattended, proceed from tool schemas and flag
the gap.

**REQUIRED BACKGROUND:** scenario-blender-expert (execution channel, review loop, 5.2 API changes).
Hair node groups (Interpolate, Clump, Curl, Hair Dynamics grooms): scenario-blender-hair.

## Stance (the expert delta)

- **A field is a deferred question, not data.** Thommes: it is evaluated by the node that consumes
  it, on that node's domain and geometry; values exist only once named or consumed. Consequence
  [added, verified]: two coupled updates (position and velocity) must be captured together in one
  Capture Attribute, or the second reads the first's new value.
- **Domain changes interpolate; everything becomes a Boolean by a rule.** Erindale: float > 0 is
  true (vectors: any non-zero), so a subdivided vertex-group selection bleeds; decide with Float to
  Integer or Compare with epsilon. Prefer trait selections (position, normal, proximity, raycast)
  over index ones, unless you generated the geometry and its order is the design (the Blender Studio
  matrix video drives a stack from Index == 0).
- **Simulation only when history matters.** Thommes: a simulation is rules applied to state; an
  animation is a function of time. If nothing depends on the previous frame, drive it from Scene
  Time and get scrubbing and sub-frames free.
- **Loops are a last resort.** Thommes: built-in nodes working on all elements use acceleration
  structures, loops cannot. For-each is for black-box generators run once per element: field
  outside, single value inside.
- **Everything is object-local.** Thommes: a (0, 0, -1) vector rotates with the object. World
  directions go through Self Object > Object Info > Invert Matrix > Transform Direction.
- **Tools, not trees.** Thommes: expose every scene dependency and tweakable value as a group input,
  never hard-reference an object inside a reusable tree, and drive gizmos only from Group Input
  sockets, through invertible math, into the first input of each math node.
- **5.2 physics is declarative.** Thommes (BCON26): forces, colliders and constraints travel as
  bundles and closures into a black-box solver. Customize from outside first (inputs, bundles,
  Custom Effector closures); make the asset local only to edit a built-in constraint. Any per-step
  custom attribute must be listed in Extra Sim Attributes, and topology-changing sims must append
  new elements at the end.

## Establish first

| Question                                                             | Why it changes the plan                                                        | Default when silent                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| What consumes the result: shader, another modifier, export, physics? | Crossing a boundary needs a named attribute; export may need realized geometry | Named attributes for anything a shader reads; keep instances |
| Does it depend on the previous frame?                                | Simulation zone and baking vs Scene Time function                              | Function of time                                             |
| One-off authoring step or reusable asset?                            | One-off may be applied (Thommes' hair noise); assets never are                 | Reusable: expose inputs, panels, sensible min/max            |
| Scale: element counts, viewport cost                                 | Realize, loops and simulations cost; instances are cheap                       | Instances, fields, no loops                                  |
| World or object space for directions and ground                      | Object-local trap                                                              | World up, world gravity                                      |

## Workflow

1. **Plan the data flow.** Name the component and domain each value lives on, where each field gets
   evaluated, and which primitive fits: plain fields first, Accumulate Field for per-group sums,
   repeat zone for N dependent passes, for-each for a black-box generator per element, simulation
   zone for state, closure to inject behavior, bundle to pass many named values. GATE: you can say
   for every field which node evaluates it.
2. **Build with `bx_gn.Builder`** (headless or live, idempotent: a tree of the same name is rebuilt
   in place). `b.node(kind, prop=..., ins={...})` sets properties before inputs, links sources,
   assigns constants; `b.zone(...)` pairs zones and adds items; `b.join([...])` keeps list order.
   GATE: `b.done()` returns (zones paired, every link created).
3. **Attach and set inputs** with `G.attach(obj, tree, inputs={...})` or `G.set_inputs(md, {...})`;
   `"attr:NAME"` switches a field input to an attribute or vertex group. GATE: `G.check(md)["ok"]`,
   no `hard_refs` on an asset.
4. **Measure.** `G.stats(obj)` (counts, attributes per domain, world bbox with instances),
   `G.attribute`, `G.instance_transforms`, `G.positions`. Then the two robustness probes: rotate the
   object 90 degrees (world-space effects keep direction) and double the input resolution (trait
   selections scale, index ones jump). GATE: numbers match the analytic expectation.
5. **Look.** `G.snapshot(objs, path, views=..., frames=...)` renders the current scene state with
   material colors and shadows (floating instances show); `bx_review.review` for realized meshes.
   Open every sheet. GATE: [`references/critique.md`](references/critique.md) visual items pass.
6. **Simulations.** Step every frame in order with `G.step(range(...))`, or `G.bake(obj)` for random
   access; assert bounds, monotonic states, counts, no NaN. GATE: a direct jump to a late frame
   equals the stepped result only after a bake.
7. **Package** (assets): inputs grouped in panels with defaults, min/max and subtypes;
   `tree.is_modifier = True; tree.asset_mark()`; drop it on a different object (Thommes' Suzanne
   test). GATE: works on the second object with no tree edit.

Recipes in [`scripts/bx_gn.py`](scripts/bx_gn.py), tested and rendered: `scatter_tree` (density x
mask, world-space slope limit, upright or aligned, pick from object and collection),
`curve_array_tree` (tangent-aligned array, alternating twist makes a chain), `growth_tree`
(repeat-zone extrusion), `particle_drop_tree` (simulation zone with emission, world gravity, ground
bounce). Prefer the shipped Essentials assets (Scatter on Surface, Array, Instance on Elements,
Randomize Transforms) when their inputs cover the brief; build your own when you need world-space
rules, masks or custom attributes.

## Quality gates

Measurable (code):

- `G.check(md)`: `ok` (no invalid link, no ERROR warning, zones paired), `hard_refs` empty for
  assets, Warning nodes you added report as expected.
- Counts match expectation: scatter count within about 12 percent of density x mask x eligible area
  [verified test]; curve array count = floor(length / spacing); repeat growth faces = F0 + sides x
  selected x iterations.
- Attributes exist on the right domain and type, values in range (`G.attribute`).
- Rotation probe and resolution probe (step 4).
- Simulation: counts per frame, bounds (nothing below the ground), prefix-stable ids when appending,
  energy or state monotonic where it must be, baked jump equals stepped.
- `G.time_eval(obj)` for hot trees; flag repeat or for-each zones in them.

Visual (`G.snapshot`, `bx_review`): scatter density reads natural and nothing floats or sinks;
arrays follow the curve without flips; growth has no self-intersection at the base; simulation strip
shows motion then rest; shader-driven attributes checked at render resolution. Gizmo feel is GUI
only.

## Common mistakes

| Mistake                                                  | What it looks like                                            | Fix                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tree.links.new` across trees                            | returns None, nothing links, no error                         | `Builder.link` raises; never reuse a bound `links.new` after switching trees |
| Setting `md.properties.inputs.<id>.value` only           | result unchanged                                              | `obj.update_tag()` (or `G.set_inputs`)                                       |
| Random Value with its implicit ID inside a for-each zone | red link, output silently wrong; `md.node_warnings` empty     | zone Index into ID; `G.check` lists `invalid_links`                          |
| Same Seed on two Random Value nodes                      | scale and rotation move together (correlation 1.0 [verified]) | offset seeds (seed + k)                                                      |
| State not wired Simulation Input to Output               | value resets each frame                                       | wire every state item through                                                |
| Custom attribute inside Cloth or Hair Dynamics           | resets every step, no warning                                 | list it in Extra Sim Attributes                                              |
| Hard-referenced controller object in an asset            | works once, breaks on reuse                                   | Object socket on the Group Input                                             |
| Coupled fields updated by two nodes                      | velocity computed from the already-moved position             | one Capture Attribute for both                                               |
| Join order assumed = link order                          | new elements inserted first, solver or ids break              | `b.join([state, new])`                                                       |
| Local direction used as world                            | effect rotates with the object                                | Self Object matrix conversion                                                |
| Closure signature by auto-population                     | ERROR "Closure does not have output"                          | create both item lists, same names                                           |

## Blender 5.2 notes

- Modifier inputs: `md.properties.inputs.<Socket_N>.value` (old `md["Socket_N"]` raises TypeError),
  then `obj.update_tag()`.
- Menus are input sockets: Transform Geometry `Mode` = 'Matrix', Resample Curve `Mode`, Custom Force
  `Mode`, Custom Effector `Stage` (menu `Socket_1`; a string input is also named Stage, `Socket_2`).
- `node.inputs["A"]` on a Mix returns the available socket in 5.2.1; duplicate enabled names
  (Cloth's two `Gravity`) still need identifiers. `bx_gn.sock` raises with the identifiers.
- Join Geometry puts the last created link first [verified].
- Evaluated `obj.bound_box` ignores instances; the instance point cloud's `position` attribute reads
  zeros, use `instance_transform` [verified]. `md.execution_time` stays 0.0 headless.
- Simulation: the first frame already runs the zone body; a jump past the cache computes one step;
  `simulation_nodes_cache_calculate_to_frame` returns PASS_THROUGH headless and computes nothing;
  `simulation_nodes_cache_bake` works (packed) [verified].
- Lists (Field to List, Get List Item), Bundles, Closures and `GeometryNodeXPBDSolver` exist; modal
  node tools do not (experimental builds only).
- Shipped assets: `<DATAFILES>/assets/nodes/geometry_nodes_essentials.blend`,
  `geometry_nodes_dynamics_assets.blend`, `procedural_hair_node_assets.blend`
  (`G.append_group(name, library)`).

# Grease Pencil (v3, Blender 5.2)

Expert Grease Pencil work keeps every drawing editable and redrawable, puts meaning in the structure
(which object, which layer, which key) and judges the result in motion. The agent draws through the
data API (drawings are curves with attributes), builds characters the way 2D studios rig them, and
reviews rendered frames instead of a viewport it cannot flip. If a sibling skill named here is
missing from your available skills, load it with `skill_get` (Scenario MCP) or ask the user to
install it (https://github.com/scenario-labs/skills#install); unattended, proceed from tool schemas
and flag the gap.

**REQUIRED BACKGROUND:** scenario-blender-expert (execution channel, review loop, 5.2 API changes).
Shot planning, boards and animatics: scenario-blender-previs-storyboard. Mesh animation principles:
scenario-blender-animation.

Toolkit: [`scripts/bx_gp.py`](scripts/bx_gp.py) (tested on 5.2.1).
`import sys; sys.path.append("<this skill>/scripts"); import bx_gp as G`.

## Stance (the expert delta)

- **Tom Viguier (Andarta, Ewilan's Quest): the rig must never block redrawing.** One GP object per
  physical element (about 60 for a lead character), parented, mostly FK by object transforms; layers
  inside each element by graphic logic (line above color); sculpting as the deformer; no armature
  weight painting on drawings, because every redraw would need new weights.
- **Tom: interpolate only "sculpted" pairs.** Two keys interpolate cleanly only with the same
  number, order and color of strokes and the same points. Otherwise redraw, or "clip" to the nearest
  drawing instead of accepting distortion. Native interpolation ignores object animation: key
  transforms separately.
- **Falk David (GP module lead): fill is geometry, not material.** A stroke fills when
  `fill_id != 0`; strokes sharing an id fill together with even-odd holes; `hide_stroke` hides the
  outline. Material fill toggles are deprecated and holdout "eraser fills" (Grant Abbitt's 4.4
  method) are obsolete.
- **Grant Abbitt: the layer stack carries meaning and materials are paint buckets.** Lines on top, a
  shadow layer (Multiply, lowered opacity, masked by the fills) in between, fills at the bottom.
  Editing a material recolors every stroke using it. Lock what you are not editing: erasers and
  sculpt act on all unlocked layers.
- **Elijah Sheffield: predictable color first.** Standard view transform, flat unlit shading, white
  world. Verified trap: new layers have `use_lights=True`, and lit layers take their ambient from
  `World.color` (default 0.05), not from the world node tree, so a flat palette renders at about a
  quarter of its value.
- **Tom: multiplane discipline and layout first.** Every 2D element parallel to the camera, a camera
  that never changes axis, 3D only where it saves time; camera, cuts and parallax are settled in
  layout, not discovered in compositing. Between objects, depth decides who draws on top.
- **Michael Weigl: motion reveals the surface.** A painterly still breaks once it moves; judge 2.5D
  as a sequence. Sort groups of strokes (mesh islands), never individual strokes, and bake
  procedural output back to editable strokes.
- **Pablo Fournier (Blender Studio): design the shadows.** Replace blobby 3D shading with blocky,
  drawn light and shadow shapes (a light and a shadow material per part). Fills are flat: use many
  small fills on curved surfaces, not one big fill pushed forward.

## Establish first

| Input          | Changes                                                                                                                                  | Default when silent                                                                                        |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Deliverable    | still, frame-by-frame shot, cutout rig, hybrid motion graphics, 2.5D over 3D                                                             | frame-by-frame shot                                                                                        |
| Format         | resolution, fps, length                                                                                                                  | 1920 x 1080, 24 fps keyed on twos [added]; social motion graphics: 1080 x 1920, 12 fps, 60 frames (Elijah) |
| Look           | flat or lit, line system                                                                                                                 | flat (unlit layers, Standard); ink line with pressure taper                                                |
| Line system    | PEN constant width (matches Line Art, Elijah) or INK_PEN pressure on radius (cartoony, Grant) or PENCIL (pressure on radius and opacity) | INK_PEN                                                                                                    |
| Palette        | material colors                                                                                                                          | hex sRGB values, one material per paint bucket                                                             |
| Camera         | ortho multiplane or perspective                                                                                                          | ortho, front view, drawing plane XZ                                                                        |
| Who edits next | how much stays procedural                                                                                                                | a human animator: everything bakes to editable strokes                                                     |

## Workflow

1. **Stage and layout.** `cam = G.scene_2d(res, fps, frame_range, ortho_scale)` (ortho camera at -Y,
   Standard, background). Plan the multiplane: which elements are separate objects and their depth
   order. Compute `px = G.px_size()`; line width in pixels is `2 * radius / px`. GATE: a test render
   shows the frame; planned line widths are at least 1.5 px [added].
2. **Structure.** `G.new_object(name, layers=("Fills", "Shadow", "Lines"))` per element (bottom to
   top, unlit), parent parts, place origins at joints. `G.material(ob, name, stroke=hex, fill=hex)`
   once per bucket. GATE: `[l.name for l in ob.data.layers]` matches intent; `G.draw_order(objs)`
   lists front to back as designed.
3. **Draw.** Keys first: `d = G.key(ob, "Lines", frame)`. Lines:
   `G.add_stroke(d, G.smooth_path(control_pts), radius, pressure=G.taper(n), brush="INK_PEN", material=i)`;
   overlap then trim rather than landing ends exactly (Grant). Fills:
   `G.add_shape(d, outline, holes=[...], material=i)` on the Fills layer, outline on Lines. Bulk:
   `G.add_strokes(d, specs)` (3000 strokes in 0.04 s). Fix shapes with `G.grab`, `G.dissolve`,
   `G.edit_op(ob, "stroke_smooth", ...)`. GATE: `G.verdict(G.report(ob))` is clean and a
   full-resolution `G.render_frame` shows no gaps, leaks or overhangs.
4. **Color and shadow.** Shadow layer: `blend_mode='MULTIPLY'`, opacity lowered, `use_masks=True`,
   `mask_layers.add(fills)`; paint the shadow shape past the edge and let the mask clip it; design
   it blocky (Pablo). Lit look: `use_lights=True` plus `World.color` as ambient plus lamps
   (verified: a sun only scales value on a flat drawing, a point light gives a gradient). GATE:
   sampled pixels match the palette under Standard.
5. **Animate.** Replacement key `G.key(..., mode="blank")`, additive `mode="copy"`, hold or cycle
   `mode="instance"` / `G.cycle(...)`, end an exposure with `G.end_exposure`. Every visible layer
   needs a key at or before `frame_start` (Elijah). Cutout motion: key object transforms (FK).
   In-betweens: check `G.match(dA, dB)`, then
   `G.interpolate(ob, layer, frame, step=2, type, easing)` (native, segment around `frame`) or
   `G.inbetween(ob, layer, a, b, frames, spacing=[...] or ease=...)` for the animator's own spacing,
   `clip=True` when the pair is different. GATE: `G.exposures(ob, layer)` per layer,
   `G.render_strip(path, frames)` read left to right for timing and pops,
   `G.onion(path, frame, before, after)` for arcs and spacing.
6. **2.5D (optional).** Outlines: `G.lineart(source, radius=width_m)` (the modifier radius is the
   line width). Strokes on meshes: `G.project_to_surface(pts, mesh)` and discard strokes with missed
   or occluder-captured points (Pablo's failure modes). Relight:
   `G.relight(ob, canvas, light_dir, shadow, light)`. Procedural strokes: Geometry Nodes Curves to
   Grease Pencil with Instances as Layers off and a `fill_id` attribute, then apply to bake
   (procedures P7). Depth reorder without changing the image: `G.push_depth(ob, delta)`. GATE: a
   moving render (strip or playblast) where the surface does not read as 3D (Weigl) and fills do not
   poke through (Pablo).
7. **Deliver.** Render frames or video with the scene camera; keep the .blend editable (no applied
   procedural stage the animator still needs). GATE: every object's verdict clean, strip and final
   frames looked at, list what was not verified.

## Numbers

| Value                                                                | Meaning                                             | Source                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `radius` = half line width (m)                                       | width px = 2 x radius / px_size                     | verified                  |
| px_size = ortho_scale / max(res_x, res_y)                            | ortho; perspective uses depth x 2 tan(fov/2) / res  | verified                  |
| 0.01 m                                                               | point radius while the `radius` attribute is absent | verified                  |
| Line Art `radius` default 0.0025 m                                   | is the line WIDTH: points get radius/2              | verified                  |
| Elijah's Line Art thickness 60 (4.x)                                 | about 0.006 m width in 5.2                          | [inferred]                |
| `use_lights` True, `World.color` 0.05                                | new layers render flat colors at about 25 % value   | verified                  |
| `set_uniform_thickness(thickness=t)`                                 | sets radius t/2                                     | verified                  |
| ~60 parts, ~100 rig versions, 2 weeks rig for a lead                 | Ewilan's Quest cutout scale                         | Tom                       |
| 12 fps, 60 frames, ortho scale 8, Subdivision 2 to 3 on shape meshes | hybrid motion graphics                              | Elijah                    |
| Stabilizer 40 px / 0.9 bundled, Elijah uses ~60 on demand            | only for long curves                                | Elijah, verified defaults |
| 1 light bounce                                                       | enough for stylized relighting                      | Weigl                     |
| GP anti-aliasing `aa_samples` 8                                      | scene.grease_pencil_settings                        | verified                  |

## Quality gates

Measurable (per object, every stage):

```python
for ob in gp_objects:
    print(ob.name, G.verdict(G.report(ob)))   # first key vs frame_start, lit-without-light,
                                             # invisible strokes, stray micro-strokes, sub-pixel lines,
                                             # fill/stroke alpha 0, empty masks; info: instances, unused materials
print(G.draw_order(gp_objects))               # front -> back vs the staging plan
print(G.match(dA, dB))                        # before any interpolation
```

Visual (open every image): `G.render_frame(path, f)` at full resolution for line quality, trims,
fill gaps and palette; `G.render_strip(path, range(a, b, 2))` for timing, holds and pops;
`G.onion(path, f, before, after)` for spacing and arcs (it includes object motion and modifiers,
which the viewport onion skin ignores, Falk and Rik); for 2.5D a sequence, never a still. Score
against [`references/critique.md`](references/critique.md).

## Common mistakes

| Mistake                                              | Looks like                                 | Fix                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Layers left at `use_lights=True` with no lamps       | flat palette renders dark brown or gray    | `layer.use_lights=False`, or raise `World.color` and add lamps |
| Fill expected from the material                      | shape outline only                         | `stroke.fill_id=1`, `cyclic=True`; holes share the id          |
| `hide_stroke=True` with `fill_id=0`                  | stroke vanishes                            | give it a fill id or show the stroke                           |
| `attributes.new("radius")` on a drawing with strokes | existing strokes disappear (radius 0)      | fill defaults first (`G.add_strokes` does)                     |
| First key after frame_start                          | drawing pops in, empty frames at the start | key at frame_start (Elijah)                                    |
| Interpolating different drawings                     | smeared, twisted in-betweens               | `G.match`; redraw, resample, or clip (Tom)                     |
| Rigging drawings with armature weights               | every redraw breaks deformation            | object-level cutout, sculpt as deformer (Tom)                  |
| Stroke-level depth sorting                           | artist's layer order destroyed             | sort groups (objects or mesh islands) (Weigl)                  |
| One big fill on a curved surface                     | fill pokes through the mesh                | many small fills near the surface (Pablo)                      |
| Deleting stray points                                | stroke splits in two                       | `G.dissolve` keeps it continuous (Pablo)                       |
| Line Art radius set like a stroke radius             | outline half the intended weight           | Line Art radius = width = 2 x stroke radius                    |
| Judging 2.5D on a still                              | looks painterly, reads as 3D in motion     | render the sequence (Weigl)                                    |
| Calling draw brushes from a script                   | `Invalid operator call`, nothing drawn     | write strokes as data; see 5.2 notes                           |

## Blender 5.2 notes

- Types: object `GREASEPENCIL`, data `bpy.data.grease_pencils`;
  `layer.frames.new(n).drawing.add_strokes([...])`; old `frame.strokes`, `point.co`, `pressure`,
  `strength`, `GPENCIL` and `object.grease_pencil_modifiers` are gone. Modifiers are regular:
  `ob.modifiers.new(n, 'GREASE_PENCIL_NOISE')`, Line Art is `'LINEART'`.
- Stroke and point helpers are Python wrappers: re-fetch after adding or removing strokes, never
  cache them.
- `grease_pencil.brush_stroke` and `sculpt_paint` have no exec: called with a stroke list in a live
  session they log "Invalid operator call" and draw nothing (verified GUI); replayed mouse events
  via `event_simulate` also drew nothing. Draw and sculpt strokes are data; headless edit operators
  (`stroke_smooth`, `stroke_simplify`, `set_uniform_thickness`, `stroke_subdivide`, `outline`,
  `join_fills`, `set_curve_type`) run in Edit mode through `G.edit_op`. In a live session
  `G.gui_trim` (lasso Trim), `G.gui_erase_box` and `G.gui_reproject(type='SURFACE')` work with a
  3D-view override.
- `interpolate_sequence` runs headless on the active object and layer, fills only the segment around
  the current frame and inserts BREAKDOWN keys; easing via `type` and `easing`.
- `frames.new` or `frames.copy` onto an existing frame raises "Frame already exists";
  `get_frame_at(n)` returns the key exposed at n (None before the first key).
- `layer.mask_layers.add(layer)` is the 5.2 mask API; layer groups `gp.layer_groups.new`,
  `gp.layers.move_to_layer_group`; layers can parent to an object or bone (`layer.parent`,
  `parent_bone`) and carry their own transform.
- Line Art objects made by `object.grease_pencil_add(type='LINEART_OBJECT')` have lit layers;
  objects hidden from render are ignored by Line Art; `lineart_bake_strokes` bakes the whole scene
  range.
- GN Curves to Grease Pencil drops plain curves while Instances as Layers is on (default); Set
  Material alone no longer fills (5.1): store an INT `fill_id` on the curve domain.

## References

- [`references/expert-notes.md`](references/expert-notes.md): each expert's principles, judgment and
  disagreements with timestamps; load when making a style or pipeline decision.
- [`references/procedures.md`](references/procedures.md): tested raw-bpy procedures (P1 to P8) and
  bx_gp recipes (cutout character, frame-by-frame, interpolation, 2.5D); load before writing GP
  code.
- `references/critique.md`: the rubric for judging line, fill, staging, timing and 2.5D renders;
  load at every review gate.
- [`references/sources.md`](references/sources.md): the five source videos, what each is best for,
  best timestamps.
